title: Creek Kids Club Extended Day Program: Workforce Solutions Child Care Services Funding Terms
content:
A Creek Kids Club Extended Day Program enrollment is funded through Workforce Solutions Child Care Services (CCS) when its third-party funder on record is Workforce Solutions Child Care Services. Every plan that accepts CCS funding takes such funding.

## Billing basis of a CCS-funded enrollment

A CCS-funded enrollment is billed at the standard rate less the board remittance. The standard monthly tuition is charged, and the board remittance posts against it.

- Its tuition charge always uses the **standard rate**, because meal-status and employee rates do not combine with CCS funding.
- The sibling discount applies only when the plan applies the sibling discount to subsidy-funded enrollments.
- Each board remittance posts as one remittance for the billing month it covers.
- The household owes the rest of that month's charges. That remainder is billed, made late and suspended like any other balance.

## When the authorization ends

When the program office records that the CCS authorization has ended, the enrollment's funder becomes none. From the next billing month posted after the change, the household's own rate basis and sibling position apply. A remittance that arrives later for a month the authorization covered still posts to that month.

## Figures by plan

| Plan | Accepts CCS funding | Billing basis for a CCS-funded enrollment |
|---|---|---|
| All six Creek Kids Club plans | yes | standard rate less board remittance (standard monthly tuition charged, board remittance posted against it) |

## Illustration (hypothetical figures)

A CCS-funded child holds a Free Meal Status and is second in the household's billing order. The month's tuition is billed at the standard rate. The free-meal rate does not apply, and no sibling discount applies, because no plan applies the sibling discount to a CCS-funded enrollment. Suppose that tuition is a hypothetical 250.00 and the board remits a hypothetical 180.00 for that month. The household owes the remaining 70.00, and that remainder is treated like any other balance for due dates, late fees and suspension.

The authorization ends in the middle of a month. The next billing month posted after that uses the household's own rate basis and sibling position. A remittance received afterwards for a month the authorization covered still posts to that earlier month.
